column1: # fact-model — Spark's canonical operative fact model (schema version 1).
# ONE machine-readable authority for the SHAPE of an operative fact: the fact
# classes an agent needs to execute a governed work unit, the envelope every
# fact is carried in, the closed status vocabulary, and the canonical
# identifier forms. reference/fact-model.md renders the same facts for a reader
# and is checked against this data (tests/test-fact-model.sh); prose is never
# This file defines HOW a fact is represented. It is NEVER an authority for
# WHAT is true: values come from their sources (GitHub, git, the repository,
# a durable human decision), and a fact only ever states what is currently
# established, with provenance pointing to why.
# FORMAT — line-oriented, tab-separated, '#'-comment and blank-line tolerant,
# the same discipline as the governance model. Records:
#   key         <class>       <canonical fact key>               (exactly one per class)
#   source-identity <type>    <regex>                            <canonical identity form for that source type>
#   source-version  <type>    <regex>                            <version-identity grammar for that source type>
#   value-shape    a machine-readable shape: {key: shape, …} is an object with exactly those keys;
#                  [shape] a list of that shape; a|b alternatives; <kind> an identifier (or the
#                  pseudo-kinds <text> = one non-empty line, <locator> = any canonical locator or
#                  source identity, <source-type> = a declared source type); a bare word is a
#                  literal (true/false are JSON booleans). The validator READS this column.
#   value-allowed  yes | no      (whether the `value` field may be present)
# EVOLUTION. `version` is the schema version every fact carries as
# `schema_version`. A consumer that reads a fact whose schema_version it does
# not know MUST treat the fact as UNKNOWN, never reinterpret field meaning.
# Nothing is added, removed or changed under an existing version: any new
# field, class, status token or vocabulary member, and any change to the
# meaning, type or requiredness of an existing one, is a NEW version. A
# consumer therefore rejects every field and class it does not know for the
# version it reads (R9 applies to the whole fact), and an older consumer can
# never accept a snapshot it cannot judge complete.
# SNAPSHOT versus FRAGMENT. A snapshot is the complete set: every `required`
# class exactly once (plus derived classes). Anything smaller is a fragment —
# useful to show one situation — and is never consumed as a snapshot.
# --- Fact classes: what an agent must know to execute a governed work unit --
# value-shape names the object the `value` field carries when ESTABLISHED.

column3: Canonical identifiers have one representation; labels, abbreviations and pretty names are projections. Each class has exactly one canonical fact key, so derived inputs and invalidation address a stable identity.
Raw issue or comment bodies, timelines and explanatory prose are not fact values; a fact points at them through provenance.
A fact states what is established now; provenance states why and how. The two are separate fields, never merged.
A derived fact lists the keys of every fact that decided it and records each input's source.version in its own source.version, so a change to any input changes and invalidates the conclusion.

Human judgment is a human-decision source with a durable record identity; it is never inferred from capability, membership, labels or cached prose. Every decision an authority value names is that fact's source.identity, so the envelope's provenance backs each grant and boundary the value carries.
value is present only when status is ESTABLISHED; UNKNOWN, CONFLICT and NOT_APPLICABLE carry no value and cannot collapse into false, null or empty.

A HEAD-bound class (head, review, checks, acceptance) that is ESTABLISHED carries its HEAD in the value and lists exactly that HEAD as its one head: invalidator; UNKNOWN or CONFLICT in a HEAD-bound class lists exactly one head: invalidator, the HEAD it was observed against; NOT_APPLICABLE lists none, because there is no HEAD to be stale against, and is invalidated by its work unit. A HEAD-bound fact is stale the moment its HEAD changes.
Two authoritative inputs that disagree are a CONFLICT with both candidates named; no first-write, last-write or plausibility rule resolves them.
A consumer that meets an unknown schema_version, an unknown class or an unknown field treats the fact as UNKNOWN; it never reinterprets or ignores what it cannot judge.
Nothing here is written to .spark/state.json; mutable GitHub execution truth is read from its source and carried in a snapshot, not stored as state.
A snapshot carries every required class exactly once; a smaller set is a fragment and is never consumed as a snapshot.
A checks fact carries exactly one result per required check name, each in the closed check-state vocabulary; merge is derivable only when every result is success.
Authority scopes and human boundaries are closed tokens carried in source-backed, targeted records; explanatory wording is provenance, never a value a consumer must interpret.

Every value has an exact shape: only the declared keys, recursively; source.identity and source.version each match the grammar of their source type; a grant names the repository or work unit it applies to. detail has the exact shape {reason, candidates} with canonical locators as candidates; acceptance item ids are scalar item-ids, unique within the fact; a work unit appears at most once per graph list.

next_action is derived, never asserted, and every fact its derivation consulted is in its inputs (so R4 re-versions it when any of them changes): merge only when the review is PASS on the current HEAD, every required check is success on it, every acceptance item is MET on it, the HEAD is current, and a grant with scope merge:routine targets the repository or work unit (review, checks, acceptance, head, authority, repository and work_unit are consulted); repair only on CHANGES REQUIRED for the current HEAD (review, head); wait-review only when no verdict binds the current HEAD or a required check is pending, missing or UNKNOWN (head, review, checks as present); stop-decision-required only when an input is CONFLICT, the verdict is DECISION REQUIRED, or boundary names a reserved boundary that applies here: the authority fact is in because and carries that boundary token with a target equal to the repository or work unit id (authority, repository, work_unit consulted), and the boundary-evidence record for that token holds on the fact it names, which is in because. boundary is none in every other case; a boundary token with no boundary-evidence record has no derivation in this version.

Every invalidator is a token in one of the invalidator grammars and appears once per fact; provenance is a pointer in the provenance grammar. Neither carries prose, so freshness and drill-down are machine-normalized.
